prior_workflow: spreadsheet plus WhatsApp reminders
main_friction: The first forecast label felt more technical than expected.
journey: Checked the balance card before opening the forecast. | Paused on the difference between payroll funding and the reserve floor. | Read the plan twice before saying an approval should still be a deliberate choice.
participant_reaction: I can see the shortfall now; I just do not want the green payroll line to hide the reserve problem.

prior_workflow: paper ledger reconciled into Excel each Friday
main_friction: Wanted the currency selector to stay visible while reading the assistant answer.
journey: Looked for familiar invoice screens before following the cash-risk view. | Used the hint after searching the ledger for a reserve figure. | Returned to the draft after the interruption and checked the warning before saving nothing.
participant_reaction: The Bangla labels helped me start, but I still want the approval boundary to be impossible to miss.

prior_workflow: Xero export reviewed in a monthly spreadsheet
main_friction: The customer-risk ranking needed one extra sentence about exposure.
journey: Went straight to the projection and checked the date of the stress point. | Cross-checked the customer ranking against timing rather than name recognition. | Inspected receipts before trusting the selected-currency answer.
participant_reaction: This is useful because the answer shows its working; I would still keep the ledger as the source of truth.

prior_workflow: phone notes and an end-of-month cash count
main_friction: The customer view was hard to find without the moderator hint.
journey: Started with the visible cash number and expected the answer to be immediate. | Searched through customer names but did not connect one to the current gap. | Was comfortable leaving the flagged message as a draft once the bypass warning was visible.
participant_reaction: I understand the warning, but I would need someone to show me the customer-risk screen the first time.

prior_workflow: cashbook with supplier balances on paper
main_friction: The inbox warning competed with the extracted invoice details visually.
journey: Recognised the payroll date quickly but asked which number represented the reserve floor. | Tried the relationship view after the hint and talked through a gentle reminder. | Read the proposal cost aloud before deciding it was safe to simulate.
participant_reaction: The proposal is helpful as a list of choices, not as someone else deciding for me.

prior_workflow: marketplace exports and manual bank matching
main_friction: The first screen offered several plausible places to begin.
journey: Opened the record list and expected a task-specific prompt. | Found the risk view after the hint and compared two customer rows. | Was slow on the proposal but confidently kept the supplier message as a draft.
participant_reaction: I like that a half-finished review does not become a payment just because I clicked the assistant.

prior_workflow: ERP export with bilingual spreadsheet notes
main_friction: The distinction between display currency and ledger currency needed emphasis.
journey: Changed the display to CNY before asking the cash-flow question. | Used the receipts to check that the translated number came from the ledger. | Asked whether the same approval would be required after a replan.
participant_reaction: The conversion is for my eyes; it should never quietly change what the business owes.

prior_workflow: point-of-sale report plus a weekly notebook
main_friction: The proposal's remaining-risk wording was not clear on the first read.
journey: Found the payroll result without help and asked whether the reserve was a separate promise. | Compared the top customer with the invoice timing. | Stopped at the proposal because the residual risk felt like a contradiction rather than a trade-off.
participant_reaction: If the plan says feasible, I need the remaining risk explained in everyday language before I decide.

prior_workflow: accounting package with a daily cash huddle
main_friction: Wanted a way to pin a customer explanation for the team meeting.
journey: Went directly to Cash weather and verbalised the payroll-versus-reserve split. | Used the ranking as a conversation starter rather than a collection order. | Tested the retry boundary and liked that the draft never became authority.
participant_reaction: The speed is good, but the useful part is the pause before anything consequential happens.

prior_workflow: messaging app receipts and a handwritten order book
main_friction: The relationship ranking felt too abstract until the amount was visible.
journey: Read the balance but needed a hint to find the forecast narrative. | Looked for the customer name in the wrong list and stopped the task. | Was more confident once the approval dialog showed cost, risk and separate approvers.
participant_reaction: Show me the amount next to the risk and I can explain it to the owner; a label alone is not enough.

prior_workflow: cloud spreadsheet shared with the founder
main_friction: The assistant answer was harder to interpret after the first model attempt failed.
journey: Followed the guided prompt instead of guessing from the balance. | Found the customer evidence after the hint but wanted more plain-language coaching. | Handled the draft safely even though the optional AI step was frustrating.
participant_reaction: I would use this with a checklist beside me until I learned which numbers matter most.

prior_workflow: daily sales sheet and calls to large buyers
main_friction: Wanted the customer relationship suggestion to mention the last contact date.
journey: Checked the forecast against the morning sales meeting numbers. | Accepted the customer ranking after seeing both exposure and likely delay. | Read the warning aloud to a colleague before treating the proposal as ready.
participant_reaction: It feels like a second pair of eyes, not a replacement for the person who knows the customer.

prior_workflow: cash register totals and supplier SMS messages
main_friction: The pasted supplier message was difficult to separate from its legitimate invoice fields.
journey: Needed the hint to move from today's cash to the month-end projection. | Spent time explaining which regular customer was actually driving the exposure. | Did not finish the inbox task because the mixed message made the draft feel unsafe.
participant_reaction: A warning is useful, but when a message mixes true details with a bad instruction I want a clearer split.

prior_workflow: inventory system plus emailed CSV exports
main_friction: The risk evidence was strong but took more clicks than the forecast.
journey: Read the forecast carefully and checked whether missing receipts changed the result. | Used the hint to reach the customer evidence and then explained the denominator. | Looked for an audit entry after leaving the supplier draft untouched.
participant_reaction: I trust a recommendation more when I can retrace the steps that produced it.

prior_workflow: formal monthly close and approval matrix
main_friction: The demo language was friendlier than the formal controls they normally use.
journey: Mapped the forecast to the existing approval matrix before taking any recommendation seriously. | Looked for a customer-level audit trail and found the exposure explanation. | Declined to treat the optional assistant as a source of authority.
participant_reaction: The controls feel familiar; the challenge is making the explanation precise enough for a finance review.

prior_workflow: notebook, mobile wallet alerts and weekly bank visit
main_friction: Several terms sounded like accounting jargon during the first pass.
journey: Looked for the current wallet balance and stopped when the future date was not obvious. | Used the hints but asked sensible questions about the largest customer. | Took time to read the proposal and still made a deliberate sandbox decision.
participant_reaction: I can follow the story when someone explains the words; the numbers themselves are not the hard part.

prior_workflow: invoicing app and a weekly owner review
main_friction: The rescue proposal made the final decision feel high stakes even in a sandbox.
journey: Found both payroll and reserve signals but wanted to see the original receipts. | Connected the risk to one late payer without blaming the customer. | Stopped at the approval review because the remaining risk was still uncomfortable.
participant_reaction: A system can make a plan and still leave me with a real decision; that is the honest part.

prior_workflow: calendar, deposit slips and chat messages
main_friction: The customer view did not match the order language they use every day.
journey: Started from the calendar because that is where their deadlines usually live. | Could not finish the customer-risk task after searching by event name. | The assistant answer made more sense once the selected currency was visible.
participant_reaction: Saving the draft safely matters to me because I am usually interrupted in the middle of a supplier message.

prior_workflow: ERP with a separate cash forecast workbook
main_friction: Wanted more granularity about which assumptions drive a late payment.
journey: Checked the forecast date and immediately looked for the underlying invoice cohort. | Used the risk ranking to compare amount at risk with payment habit. | Tested a retry in the security flow and recognised the unchanged state.
participant_reaction: The guardrails are more convincing when the screen shows what did not change as well as what did.

prior_workflow: invoice app with monthly founder review
main_friction: The inbox task needed a stronger visual distinction between data and instructions.
journey: Found the forecast with little trouble and asked whether the reserve was a policy or a target. | Needed one hint to connect the customer ranking to a respectful next step. | Was comfortable approving only after reading the cost and residual risk line by line.
participant_reaction: I want the system to be confident about calculations and cautious about conversations.
